The word “Stereo” is on the interface and then changes to “M/S”. The presenter changes the EQ settings on what is marked as the side, adding a peak to the high frequencies of the sound. There is a menu visible with options such as "Save as Default Preset", "Copy A > B", "Copy B > A", "Reset All Gains", and "Hi-Quality" (High-Quality), indicating potential functions for customizing or adjusting EQ parameters. The background features the DAW’s arrangement view, indicating the track and timeline where the EQ plugin is applied. The significant visual change is the transition from 'Stereo' to 'M/S' mode and the adjustment of EQ nodes on the frequency graph, demonstrating how to shape the audio's spectral content.

Here's a breakdown of what I see in the video segment:
The video showcases a digital audio workstation, specifically Ableton Live, where the user provides tips and tricks for manipulating audio and midi, the person is not visible. Initially, the screen displays the interface of Ableton Live with waveforms and settings. In the Live Devices section, viewers are advised on using the "Driver Error Compensation" tool for audio interface latency issues. Subsequently, the video demonstrates the creation of LFOs (low-frequency oscillators) for arbitrary parameters within the software, including the creation of unlinked looping envelopes. The user then showcases the "warp modes," which can be used to repitch audio clips, including achieving male-to-female vocal transpositions. Lastly, the "beats mode" is highlighted as a way to create tremolo-type effects and shows the default setting for warping audio. Text appears in the frames, mainly labels for settings and parameters in the software such as: “Dry/Wet”, “Latency”, “Transpose”, “Driver Error Compensation”, etc. All are in English. Overall, the video offers a tutorial-style guide with a focus on advanced audio manipulation and routing tips.
